author: rcmacf
text:
Here's how I am marking in the PAZs, based on my current understanding. I'm leaving out cpPAZ until I've got a handle on the FTR PAZ. I'm using the same chart area as above, so we've consistency. Peds, am I getting there?

1. First I mark in the FTRs I see. These I take to be an engulf (a new high in this case) showing intent to go higher, then the fail to go lower. It does not become a true FTR until price then moves higher than the initial higher high. So, for example, z does not qualify as an FTR as y is a few pips lower than x. (it is a cpPAZ edge, but I'm not going near those yet). I've used a little red ellipse to show the tips of the FTRs.

2. I then mark in the demand zones (or supply if moving down) which the FTRs represent. My indi marks those created above current price blue, and those below as pink). These are going to become the targets on the way down - the FTB to the FTR, essentially.

3. Then it's a case of watching what price does:

The engulf at 1 means expect price to go to 2 (engulf 1 also engulfs an FL to the left of the top elipse, and should have you primed and ready for point A to happen - it is ignored demand becoming supply - an SR flip).

The engulf at 3 means expect price to go to 4

The engulf at 5 means expect price to go to 6, whichever PAZ edge that leads to next. If you were sharp, you could maybe get in at B.

And see how the influence continues..

Hi yalanola

I'm learning PAZ and FTR too in these days.

As a beginner I think that your trade is reasonable, we are in supply zone in many timeframes, previous low and important key level is engulfed on H4, previous highs respected, right now no sign that price wants to go higher to me. Let's see what happens next..

I didn't understand very well how did you draw your PAZ and FTR and how you used PAZ and FTR concepts to enter that trade.

Here I tryed to draw some PAZ and FTR, any comment and suggestion is welcome.

If I understand correctly, one option to trade PAZ and FTR is: once a previous FTR is engulfed, we entered in a new PAZ between 2 FTRs. So the price wants to go to the other side of the PAZ where the next FTR Supply or Demand zone is. What we want to do is search for a SD area near the origin of the move that engulfed previous FTR and enter on the retracement. I found 2 problems doing this: 1) Many times (like in my example) price doesn't retrace or do only a little retracement not giving us a clear entry point and a good R:R 2) If the price engulfs a FTR and then touch the next at the other side of the PAZ and then retraces to the origin, this PAZ is not tradable because price already reached the other side.

Is it correct?

author: yalanola
text:
Hi, Andy,

My understanding on the FTR set-up is when price breaks out a level, it may comes back to get more orders in order to gain the momentum, it either hit the break-though point (called retest) or doesn't even made it back to the point (FTR) and then turns in the direction. I understand that this would be the decision point. There might be some orders left there, so when the price reaches the level again, which is the FTB, it may pick up those orders and this creates an entry opportunity. I feel that some of your marks are not exactly FTR, the most obvious one is at the top where you marked "supply". when price dropped from "newer hight" you marked, it attempted to come back, but failed, from there, the price goes all the way down to "CP" you marked, so, that area will be your reference, when the price comes back to that level. You would take short opportunity from there.

I'll post chart afterwards and let'd discuss about it.

Cheers.

author: Andyfx
text:
In my view a FTR is created when something (a previous High/Low, a Key Level, a previous FTR, a previous SD zone like RBR/DBD) gets engulfed and there is a pullback.

I think that most of the FLs are FTR too, because they form when a SR level gets engulfed and in the flag there is actually a pullback, an attempt to return to the origin of the move, so we can call it FTR.

But why not all FL are FTR? Well, if I understand FLs, most of the times a flag forms after a SR level gets engulfed, so we can call it FTR, but in some FLs the flag forms BEFORE the SR gets engulfed, so this flag has not yet engulfed something right now, so we can't call it FTR, in this case the real FTR is the FTB to the flag limit. Look at the draw below.

Decision points are FTR? Same as I said about FLs, most DP are FTR too, but not all. Imagine a Rally-Base-Rally that forms in the middle of nowhere and there is no engulf of previous things, is this a decision point? Yes, when the flag breaks there is the decision to go higher. Is this a FTR? No, because no engulf.

Makes sense?

Anyways don't take it for true, I'm just a noob in the market, maybe I'm wrong!
